deduplication: Read all 446 current general definitions before adding this manifest. No LiuPi identity, liu-pi manifest or ol:yicheng skill was registered; the similarly named Yicheng of other characters is a different skill.

currentClient.decoder: Fetched public bundle ZIP in memory, read its actual InitOfb IV/key, decoded Config character.sgs and cha_spell.sgs using that AES-CFB128 implementation followed by gzip. No guessed key, no persisted runtime/config files.

spellRow.o: 出牌阶段限一次，你可以展示牌堆顶X张牌（X为你的体力上限），然后可以用任意张手牌交换其中等量张牌，若展示牌点数之和因此增加，你可以用所有手牌交换展示牌。

primarySemantics: Reveal count is current maximum HP at activation, not current HP. The initial exchange pays and obtains exactly the same number of physical cards.
The second optional exchange requires a strict increase of the displayed cards' actual rank sum caused by that first exchange; equality and decline do not qualify.
The second exchange exchanges the entire current hand and entire displayed set; these two set sizes need not be equal. Neither exchange is a discard cost.

secondaryOperationalEvidence.status: Secondary gameplay guide; not an independent official FAQ or quote of server rules.
observations: Displayed cards return to the draw-pile top after resolution, rather than following Mubing's reveal-to-discard disposition.
The first exchange preserves displayed positions and replaces selected positions with selected hand cards in their existing hand arrival order.
The optional second all-hand exchange permits arranging the outgoing hand order on top. The local UI exposes an explicit private order selection without enumerating permutations.

implementation: Pending choices and immutable table/payment/order receipts live on the owning ProgramSkillFrame, with exact last movement ordinals rejecting an entity that left and returned to Processing.

Both physical exchange directions use one native atomic movement batch, preserving receipts, movement triggers and final hand counts. Each public table update uses the existing deep-frozen ProgramCardsRevealedEvent.

The first rank comparison freezes at the committed exchange, before nested observers can change hand/table state. The second exchange captures the actual whole hand after first-exchange children finish.

Semantic inference for nested intervention: cards removed by a real observer are no longer available merely because the same entity later returns to Processing; only uninterrupted displayed receipts participate in cleanup or subsequent exchange.
